source.extraction_method: Manual extraction from current TypeScript behavior; every rule below is labelled implementation-derived and cites the implementation lines used.
source.determinism: Do not include timestamps. Update only when current TypeScript behavior or measured feedback-loop metrics change.

rules.label: implementation-derived
rules.rule: Default layout uses 150 px column pitch, spine Y=70, lower tracks at Y=210 and Y=490, 140 px track gap, and nominal channels at Y=140/280/560 before dynamic channel planning.

rules.label: implementation-derived
rules.rule: Events are 36x36, gateways 50x50, expanded subprocesses 360x200, and all other node types default to 100x80.

rules.label: implementation-derived
rules.rule: Sequence flows whose source or target belongs to a different immediate process/subprocess container are rejected before layout; existing BPMN diagrams are then removed and regenerated per process.

rules.label: implementation-derived
rules.rule: A DFS marks back-edges as loop-backs. The primary spine starts at the first start event and follows non-back-edge outgoing flows, scoring end events high, subprocesses and reject/error/fail/give-up branches low, and looping targets lower than completion exits.

rules.label: implementation-derived
rules.rule: Spine nodes occupy track 0 and increasing columns. Branches are placed breadth-first relative to their parent; exception branches go upward, ordinary non-spine branches go downward unless a loop-back spans the gateway, and same-track nodes are shifted to avoid width-based overlap.

rules.label: implementation-derived
rules.rule: When an upper track exists, it becomes the visual spine; lower tracks are offset from the default track pitch. Tracks containing nodes taller than 80 px add cumulative vertical clearance.

rules.label: implementation-derived
rules.rule: Expanded subprocesses keep the 360x200 outer box and lay child flow nodes left-to-right inside the box with 35 px leading padding and 60 px horizontal gaps.

rules.label: implementation-derived
rules.rule: Disconnected top-level components are packed after local layout, either below or beside the main start-event component, using a 100 px component gap and a landscape A4 aspect-ratio score. Node center X values are then snapped to the 75 + n*150 grid when the move is at most 20 px.

rules.label: implementation-derived
rules.rule: Loop-back and bypass channels are derived from the occupied node band with 40 px clearance. Overlapping channel spans are assigned separate 30 px lanes using a two-pass greedy plan before final waypoints are emitted.

rules.label: implementation-derived
rules.rule: Waypoint routing handles subprocess-internal flows, gateway-to-gateway upside bypasses, loop-backs, same-track forward flows, gateway branches up/down, merges into gateways, and a final orthogonal fallback.

rules.label: implementation-derived
rules.rule: Crowded node-side attach points are fanned out deterministically by flow id. Routed polylines are repaired by enforcing outward departure, treating nearby node and existing-path rectangles as obstacles, trying visibility routes and ordered 15 px nudges up to 300 px, and side-approaching blocked final legs.

rules.label: implementation-derived
rules.rule: Named events and gateways receive external BPMNLabel bounds. Candidate label positions vary by flow attachment directions, gateway shape, preferred top/bottom side, text width, and line count; candidates that collide with lanes, elements, or previously placed labels are rejected before fallback.

rules.label: implementation-derived
rules.rule: The current label solver uses an 8 px primary/alternate vertical gap for named events and a 0 px gap for named gateways; collision-free candidate selection can choose a different side or offset. This is a generalized parameterized heuristic, but the desired gateway-above versus gateway-below preference is not yet a complete formal rule.

rules.label: implementation-derived
rules.rule: Named sequence flows receive labels on a preferred horizontal segment of at least 30 px, or otherwise a vertical segment of at least 20 px. Edge labels are placed before node labels so node-label placement can avoid them.

rules.label: implementation-derived
rules.rule: ensureLabelDi materializes default BPMNLabel rectangles for named events, gateways, and lanes when shape DI exists but label bounds do not; event/gateway defaults are 90x20 below the shape, and lane defaults are a 30 px tall rectangle rotated into the lane boundary.

rules.label: implementation-derived
rules.rule: labelLayout reports missing label DI for named events/gateways/lanes, invalid label bounds, lane labels outside lane bounds, labels overlapping elements or labels, and labels outside containing lanes or participants.

metrics.definition: Counts BPMN XML elements by local name plus sequence flows, message flows, lanes, and data references for fixture coverage and regression slicing.
Computes diagram extents from shape bounds and edge waypoints as x, y, width, and height.
Counts non-container shape overlaps, total shape overlap area, and label-label overlaps from BPMN DI bounds.
Counts edge crossings, edge intersections with non-endpoint non-container shapes, total bends, Manhattan length, and non-orthogonal segments.
Measures non-container shape center-X deviation from the implementation grid 75 + n*150, reported as average and maximum absolute deviation.
Compares named events, gateways, lanes, sequence/message flows, and data references against BPMN DI labels, reporting covered and missing label targets.

Reports count, minimum, maximum, and average vertical gap between named event/gateway shapes and their BPMNLabel bounds, grouped by element class. Use this to compare gateway labels with the 8 px event-label baseline.

feedback_observations.status: candidate heuristic, not yet promoted to implementation rule
feedback_observations.observation: The overall three-row grid, happy-path spine, branch spacing, event-subprocess alignment, and label-to-node distances are good. The exclusive gateway label 'Order valid?' could use a slightly larger below-node gap; the above-node labels 'Check in parallel' and 'Checks complete' could use a small consistent gap comparable to event labels.
feedback_observations.next_step: Use metric.labels.node_label_gap and visual reports on multiple gateway orientations before changing the shared gap parameter.

loop: Run the report command to capture original/transformed images and deterministic metrics.
Collect feedback JSON with checkbox choices, Likert ratings, and comments.
Map low ratings and selected choices to this ruleset and the report metrics.
Change TypeScript behavior, update this artifact from the changed implementation, and rerun targeted reports.
